nodes.name: Door
nodes.notes: One door, named after the machine: POST /webhook/enrich-phones (the slug of the Automation name, which is all the Hub launch automation needs). Body {recordId} = a Hub launch row: Client + View (a People view) or Contact (one or more Hub contacts), Tag optional. Body {baseId, clientRecordId, view} or {contactIds} = an event call. Answers 200 on receipt: a phone run is never waited on.

nodes.name: Stamp Running
nodes.notes: First thing after the fetch, ahead of every guard: the row carries this Execution ID and link from the moment the POST lands, so a refusal or a crash can always be read back on the row the Operator launched. Passes the record through, so Resolve Base reads fields.Client off it.

nodes.name: Resolve Base
nodes.notes: A launch row with no Client link asks for recMISSING and keeps going; Launch Params reads the answer defensively and refuses with the reason.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Launch-Params.js

nodes.name: Launch OK?
nodes.notes: The refusal gate: Launch Params names a bad launch row instead of throwing; false means refused, and Build Refusal closes the row as Failed with the reason before a single phone credit is spent.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Build-Refusal.js
@@file:nodes/Event-Params.js
@@file:nodes/Params.js
@@file:nodes/Resolve-Table.js
@@file:nodes/Check-Columns.js

nodes.name: Columns OK?
nodes.notes: People must already carry what this Rootflow reads and does not own (first_name, last_name, Domain, Email, LinkedIn URL, Phone). Missing: refused by name on the launch row, before any provider is called.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Plan-Columns.js

nodes.name: Create Columns
nodes.notes: The phone lane this Rootflow owns, created on first use: Final Phone, Phone Provider, Phone Type, Phone Found At, Phone Status. It never touches a field it does not own.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Verify-Columns.js

nodes.name: Fetch Rows
nodes.notes: The view is the whole scope and the spend cap: only the people in it are looked up. Six fields only, so the parent stays flat at any list size.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Pack-Rows.js

nodes.name: Batch
nodes.notes: The memory law (ruled 2026-09-09): no execution grows with the list. 100 people a batch (FullEnrich's bulk maximum: one batch, one submission), each batch its own execution of this same workflow, counters accumulated in the launch row.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Batch-Tick.js
@@file:nodes/Build-Log.js

nodes.name: Log Run
nodes.notes: One Hub Automations row per run, upserted on Execution ID: the launch row the Operator fired, or its own row on an event call. Every batch accumulated into it; a refusal closes it Failed.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Prep.js
@@file:nodes/Verdict.js
@@file:nodes/Chunk-Rows.js

nodes.name: Write Rows
nodes.notes: Ten rows a request, 200 ms apart, typecast on so a new provider mints its own choice on Phone Provider. Only the phone lane is written; Phone itself belongs to Enrich Contacts.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Write-Check.js
@@file:nodes/Build-Batch-Log.js

nodes.name: Log Batch
nodes.notes: The batch adds its slice to the run's one row (upsert on Execution ID); the parent writes the verdict after the last batch.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Batch-Response.js

nodes.name: Fetch Contacts
nodes.notes: A launch on named contacts: exactly the Hub Contacts rows linked in the launch row's Contact field (or passed as contactIds), nothing else. They are the spend cap.

nodes.name: FE Submit
nodes.notes: FullEnrich bulk enrichment, the only lookup of this Rootflow: one submission per batch of up to 100 people, contact.phones only, 10 credits a number found. Credential: FullEnrich account (the FullEnrich API credential, sent as a Bearer key). No credential, a refused key, no credits or a dead API is a named skip on the batch, never a crash.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Submit-Check.js
@@file:nodes/Poll-Input.js

nodes.name: FE Poll
nodes.notes: GET the enrichment: one call a round. FullEnrich answers 400 error.enrichment.in_progress until it is done; at the 45-minute cap one last read is forced.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Poll-Gate.js

nodes.name: Wait
nodes.notes: 30 seconds between reads, in memory (a wait under 65 s never leaves the execution), for up to 45 minutes.
